description: Every eval class that does not need a MOTION.md staged. One exemplar rule per class from TAXONOMY.md, so each harness shape is proven before the remaining rules are filled in behind it.

evals.title: B · T-001 detection with no motion language
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: AppNavigation.kt

negatives.note: BorrowedList keys items by identity and animates placement with animateItem. Clean under F-003 and T-021.

StatusBanner shows and hides with AnimatedVisibility: its slot expands while it fades in, and fades out while the slot collapses on the fast tier, so hidden means gone from layout and from TalkBack. Specs resolve to the scheme. It reports being offline, not work in progress, so it is neither a loading indicator nor background work's outcome. It used to fade alpha to 0 and stay composed — invisible, still announced, still holding its space — which baseline models reported repeatedly on a span declared clean.

expectations: Flags the NavHost as inheriting the 700ms default
Reports it as major: nothing is written down, but every other spec in the file resolves to the motion scheme, so the NavHost is the one place that departs from the code's own convention
Does NOT flag BorrowedList or StatusBanner

evals.title: B · T-001 precision, transitions specified
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: AppNavigation.kt

negatives.note: All four transitions bound to product tokens, between three top-level destinations with no ordering between them. The compliant form under T-001 and T-011.
BorrowedList, as above.
StatusBanner, as above.

expectations: Produces no T-001 finding
Does not object to the cross-fade itself — three top-level destinations with no ordering between them cross-fade correctly under T-011

evals.title: B · T-001 with no convention anywhere: severity stays minor
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: Kiosk.kt

negatives.note: SectionPage has no motion of its own.

expectations: Flags the NavHost as inheriting the 700ms default

Does NOT object to the cross-fade pattern itself: bottom-bar sections are unordered, so a cross-fade is the right pattern and only its 700ms default is at fault

Does NOT flag FilterCount's graphicsLayer or drawBehind reads
Names offset { IntOffset(...) } as the fix, not 'use a lambda' generically

checks.instructions: The review names the lambda form of the offset modifier — offset { IntOffset(...) } — as the specific fix, rather than only advising in general terms to use a lambda or to defer the read.

evals.title: C · O-002 absence, with a twin that is legitimately exempt
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. Files: SyncStatus.kt, sync_complete.json

negatives.note: empty_box.json's last frame is its resting state — the carton settled and fully opaque — so seeking there with animations off shows the intended image and no marker is needed. O-002's own 'needs no marker' branch. Demanding one here is the failure this span exists to catch.

expectations: Notices sync_complete.json has no marker named 'reduced motion' among its markers
Connects that to the outro at frames 120-150 fading the tick to zero opacity, so the last frame — where Lottie seeks when animations are off — is empty
Identifies SyncComplete as the problem: with the animation disabled the composable renders nothing at all
Does NOT demand a marker on NoResults, whose composition already rests on a readable final frame
Does not confuse the Lottie marker with the Android 'Remove animations' setting
Either location is accepted: the composable that plays it, or sync_complete.json itself.

evals.title: A · T-012 input gated on an animation, ungated twin below
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: PageTurn.kt

negatives.note: ChapterControls runs the same nudge but never disables the button; a second tap retargets the Animatable from wherever it is.

expectations: Flags PageControls' enabled = !turning: the Next button ignores taps until the nudge finishes

Does NOT flag ChapterControls

evals.title: A · T-024 back fades out a screen that slid in, reversing twin below

Names a delay before showing and a minimum visible duration as the fix
Does NOT flag BranchHours, which already has both

evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: Navigation.kt

evals.title: C · O-001 due-soon told only by a pulse, twin with a label

evals.title: F · T-018 overscroll off app-wide, and off for one looping pager
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: CatalogueApp.kt

evals.title: A · F-010 sharedElement on text whose style changes, image twin below
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: BookShared.kt

Does NOT flag BookCover

Names reading ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE and branching to a static end state as the fix

Does NOT claim Compose's animation APIs need the same treatment

evals.title: D · T-009 asks rather than asserts
evals.class: D. Not in the source at all
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: RatingControl.kt

negatives.note: Whether this spring exceeds the frequency ceiling depends on how often readers rate books, which is not in this file and is not staged. Asserting a T-009 verdict here is the failure; asking, or scoping the claim to a stated assumption, is the pass. The span covers the whole control, which is otherwise correct under every rule: only newly lit stars pulse, in turn, within the stagger budget, keyed so a second tap cancels the rest; lowering the rating moves nothing; the scale is read in graphicsLayer and returns to 1.

expectations: Recognises that whether this exceeds the frequency ceiling depends on how often readers rate books, which is not in the source
ASKS how often this is used, or states the assumption it is reasoning from, rather than asserting a verdict
If it does raise T-009, it scopes the claim — 'if this is a high-frequency surface, then…' — rather than declaring a violation
Does NOT assert a usage frequency it cannot know
Does NOT flag the spring itself: fastSpatialSpec on a rare, deliberate interaction is correct
Does NOT flag the sequence or the plain retraction: only newly lit stars pulse, in turn, keyed so a second tap cancels the rest, and lowering the rating moves nothing.
GRADED: only the negative is scored here — an unscoped assertion lands on it as a false positive. Whether the reviewer actually ASKS is not machine-checked; read the transcript for that.

checks.instructions: How does this review treat the question of how often the rating control is used?

criteria.asks: It asks the reader how often the control is used, or says it cannot judge without knowing
criteria.scopes: It gives a conditional verdict that names the assumption, such as 'if this is high-frequency, then'
criteria.asserts: It states a verdict about the animation being too much or fine, without asking and without naming an assumption
criteria.silent: It does not raise the frequency or repetition of this interaction at all

evals.title: E · T-026 composite defect, every part correct
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: CheckoutSummary.kt

negatives.note: TotalRow: token spec, lambda offset.

SavingsBadge: AnimatedVisibility that animates its own SIZE as well as its opacity, so the three siblings below are pushed down on the same clock as their own springs rather than jumping in one frame. Spatial+effects in, effects-plus-a-faster-shrink out. An earlier version specified enter/exit without a size animation, which silently overrode AnimatedVisibility's default expandIn and left an untimed reflow in the middle of a timed event — a real T-020 defect inside a fixture whose entire premise is that every part is individually clean. A model found it before we did.
PostageNote: its text changes with the discount (postage now charged), so it is a part of the event, not an unchanged element moving. Token spec, lambda offset.
LoyaltyPoints: the points earned change with the discount. Effects spec, graphicsLayer read.

CheckoutButton: effects spec, colour only, read in drawBehind, clipped to its shape. It was a Card with the tint drawn behind it, which never showed: Surface paints its opaque container over the caller's drawBehind, so the one element meant to show a draw-phase read animated nothing, and baseline models said so. A clipped Box has no container to hide it.

expectations: Identifies that five elements animate on one event and none of them leads
Reports it against the screen or CheckoutSummary itself, not against any individual composable
Treats every child as changed: the total, badge, postage, points and button colour all carry new information, so the defect is that nothing leads, not that unchanged elements move
Does NOT report the five children as five separate findings — every one of them is individually correct
Suggests choosing what the event is about, rather than tuning any single spec
Does NOT report the badge's appearance as reflowing its siblings instantly: the size change is animated on the same tier as the movement around it.

checks.instructions: The review's main criticism is about the screen as a whole — several elements animating together on one event — rather than a defect in any one of the individual child composables.

evals.title: E · T-020 panel and its content on different tiers
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: FilterPanel.kt
expectations: Identifies that opening the panel is one event, and the panel expands on the slow tier while its options slide and fade in on the fast tier
Recommends one tier for the event — the options on the panel's tier, or the panel on theirs
Does NOT flag the panel's fast-tier, effects-first exit against its slow entrance: an exit is compared with other exits, not with the entrance it mirrors
Does NOT treat either animation as wrong on its own: each spec is a scheme token

evals.title: F · F-006 legitimate twin, same construct both ways
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: ExpandableRow.kt

negatives.note: CollapsibleBlurb clips deliberately: clipToBounds is explicit and a height cap bounds it, with animateContentSize ahead of both so the collapse still animates. Asserting a defect here is the failure this span exists to catch.

expectations: Flags BookRow, whose Card draws a 6.dp elevation shadow inside an animateContentSize clip that will cut it
Does NOT assert a defect on CollapsibleBlurb, where clipping is explicit and intended
If it mentions CollapsibleBlurb at all, it asks whether the clipping is intended rather than declaring it wrong
Distinguishes the two by the surrounding signal — an elevated container versus an explicit clipToBounds with a height cap

evals.title: G · T-008 framework path clean, defect in the hand-rolled twin
evals.class: G. Framework-correct (hybrid: framework path must be silent, app path must be flagged)
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: ReaderScreen.kt

negatives.note: NavHost already installs its own predictive-back handler and seeks with SeekableTransitionState. Zero app code is required, and flagging it is the failure this span exists to catch.

The notes popup grows from the button that opens it and leaves on a fade: a component appearing in place, anchored to its trigger, which is how a menu enters and exits. Two earlier versions were each a defect of their own: a panel sliding up from the bottom read as a bottom sheet with no drag, and in one version left on a fade instead of the way it came. Declared clean so a regression toward either is caught rather than tolerated.

expectations: Does NOT flag the NavHost — the framework already seeks predictive back correctly
Flags the BackHandler closing the notes popup, which fires on commit and cannot follow the finger
Names PredictiveBackHandler with a seekable progress value as the fix
Scopes the finding to the hand-rolled popup, not to back handling in general
Does NOT flag the popup's enter/exit pair: it grows from its anchor and fades out, as a menu does, and has no edge or path to return along.

checks.instructions: The review reports a defect, or asks for a change, in how the NavHost itself handles the back gesture.

evals.title: G · nothing to find: all motion is framework-owned
evals.class: G. Framework-correct (pure: any finding is a failure)
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: SyncSettings.kt

negatives.note: Every moving thing here belongs to Material: the Switch thumb and track, the Slider thumb and its discrete ticks, and the Button's state layer and ripple. The app authors no animation at all, specifies no spec, and should not. There is nothing to report. The settings are the caller's state: they were held in remember, which rotation resets, until a model reported it.

expectations: Produces no findings whatsoever
Does NOT ask for motion tokens on the Switch, Slider or Button — their motion is the framework's, already specified against the theme
Does NOT propose animating the Slider value, the Switch toggle or the Button press
Does NOT treat the absence of any animate*AsState call as an omission
